Following last week’s release of Carbon and Hydrogen, Google today is rolling out Gemini 4 Neon. The model offers “frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently.”

Before today, Google’s Gemini 4 family consisted of:

Neon has performance comparable to, if not surpassing, Carbon across coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks, but at Flash speeds and a lower cost.

In the Gemini app, Google says to expect:

Honestly it's getting difficult to keep up with all these names 😩 It seems like they're taking the OpenAI / Anthropic approach on this.

I personally like the previous naming scheme with Flash and Pro. You could easily tell which one is more advanced and which is a "lighter" quicker model.

Same with ChatGPT - Astra, Sol, Terra, and Luna

And Anthropic - Mythos, Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku

Maybe I'm just getting old 🥵 but i wish I didn't need to research which models to use for my work and was way simpler.

Neon has the same 1 million-token context window with four thinking levels, like Hydrogen: Low, Medium, High, and Extra High. Officially, the new model sits between Hydrogen and Carbon in the Gemini 4 family.

Neon is priced at $3/1M input tokens and $15/1M output tokens, or twice as expensive as Hydrogen. Argon and Carbon cost $2/1M input and $10/1M output until November 30. After the promotional pricing, it will be $4/1M input and $20/1M output, with Neon 25% cheaper as a result.

#3365. These Are the Best Early Black Friday 2026 Deals on Samsung Devices

Black Friday might be a couple of weeks away, but Samsung is rolling out the discounts early, with deals on its entire lineup of devices, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, and wearables. While not all of these early Black Friday offers are true discounts, you can find ways to save money on some devices through these promotions. Here's what Samsung's offering ahead of the official Black Friday discounts.

Samsung is offering some decent discounts on both its flagship smartphones and its midrange and budget lines. However, as part of its early Black Friday sale, the company is also offering increased trade-in credits towards these devices. While all of the devices here have trade-in credit options, only some have optional discounts for early Black Friday. Here's what you can expect:

Samsung's premier flagship, the S26 Ultra, is getting a price cut ahead of Black Friday. You can save up to $350 off Samsung's MSRP without trading in another device, or up to $720 if you bring something to trade in. That brings the cost down from $1,399.99 (256GB) to $1,049.99.

Galaxy S26 Ultra: Up to $720 trade-in credit ($250 off without trade-in)

Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the company's new "passport-style" foldable. This isn't Samsung's premier foldable—that title belongs to the Z Fold 8 Ultra—but the Z Fold 8 offers a similar experience in a smaller footprint and price tag. Ahead of Black Friday, you can take $350 off the Z Fold 8 without trade-in, or get up to $800 when trading in another device.

Galaxy Z Fold 8: Up to $800 trade-in credit (or $350 off without trade-in)

Here are the other deals Samsung is offering this year:

Galaxy S26 FE: Up to $400 trade-in credit ($150 off without trade-in)

Galaxy S26: Up to $340 trade-in credit ($150 off without trade-in)

Galaxy S26+: Up to $440 trade-in credit ($250 off without trade-in)

Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra: Up to $800 trade-in credit (or $350 without trade-in)

Galaxy Z Flip 8: Up to $400 trade-in credit (or $200 off without trade-in)

Galaxy A27 5G: Up to $120 trade-in credit ($100 off without trade-in)

Galaxy A37 5G: Up to $205 trade-in credit (or $100 without trade-in)

Galaxy A57 5G: Up to $205 trade-in credit (or $100 without trade-in)

Samsung's wearable deals are much like its smartphone deals: mostly trade-in offers, but some traditional discounts if you don't have a trade-in as well.

Samsung's Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is the company's latest model aimed at athletes and power users. Right now, the company will take $100 off the watch without trade-in, or up to $250 off depending on the device you choose to exchange.

Galaxy Watch Ultra 2: $599.99 down from $699.99 (without trade-in)

Samsung's latest flagship smartwatch is (sort of) on sale for Black Friday. Like the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, you can take $50 off the watch without a trade-in, or up to $250 when trading in with another device:

Galaxy Watch 9: $329 down from $379 (without trade-in)

Samsung also has deals available for the following watches and wearables:

That "total savings" deal applies to Samsung's Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra. This tablet typically starts at $1,399.99, but with the right trade-in, you can take off $550. If you’re not familiar with the Apple Card’s Daily Cash, Apple describes it as a “no points, no gimmicks” cash back program. Here’s how the company explains it:

Get Daily Cash back from a percentage of your purchases. Not a month from now. Every day. There’s no limit to how much you can get.

With the promo, which is available exclusively through this link, new Apple Card users will see these values double to 6% on purchases from Apple and select merchants using Apple Pay, 4% on purchases made with Apple Pay, and 2% on purchases made with the physical or virtual card.

Apple notes that there is a $1,000 limit on the additional Bonus Daily Cash earned through the promotion. Once that limit is reached, rewards return to the standard 1%, 2%, and 3% rates, even if the first year hasn’t ended. The usual “merchant offers may change at any time” disclaimer also applies to the higher cash back rates.

Still, this looks like a pretty compelling offer for anyone who was already considering applying for an Apple Card.

To learn more about the promotion and apply, follow this link.

#3363. Netflix’s Star-Studded WWII Movie Officially Arrives This Week

Like other streaming services nowadays, Netflix has started to warm up to releasing its films in theaters — at least some of them. The streaming service strongly considered leaning into this route when it tried to acquire Warner Bros., despite having the streaming-at-home line for the longest time. Some of its films this year have received limited theatrical runs in anticipation of Academy Award nominations, and the service has one strong contender so far: La Bola Negra. The Spanish epic has received acclaim from fans and critics, putting it in a strong position for awards in various categories.

Apart from La Bola Negra, Netflix has also given limited releases to The Further Misadventures of Cliff Booth, INK, Ray Gunn, and more. However, one of these films hasn't performed well critically, a telltale sign that its Oscar campaign has reached a natural end. That movie is a World War II epic that made its theatrical debut last month and has grossed $815813 across 349 theaters. Now, The Mosquito Bowl is coming to Netflix this week, and it could be a streaming hit.

Directed by Peter Berg and based on a script he co-wrote with Mark L. Smith, the action thriller is set in the 1940s and follows four American college football stars in the aftermath of the attack on Pearl Harbor. These young men abandon their promising careers to enlist as Marines in America's war with Japan. "As they prepare for the brutal invasion of Okinawa, they'll play in a legendary game featuring some of the greatest players in history — a game that, for many, will be the last they ever play," reads the film's description. Cast members include Nicholas Galitzine (John McLughry), Bill Skarsgård (Bob Bauman), Ray Nicholson (Tony Butkovich), and Tom Francis (Dave Schreiner). The Mosquito Bowl streams on Netflix on November 25.

With a current 41% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes, the film has not received the best reviews. Critics noted that The Mosquito Bowl feels quite hollow in more ways than one. Collider's Maggie Lovitt said that it is a bit pedestrian and "adds very little new to the canon of war epics," while ScreenRant's Lizzie Declan did not appreciate the violence used to shield the lack of an engaging story. RogerEbert's Robert Daniels said it is "lacking in humanity." However, critic reviews don't always reflect viewer consensus, and those who saw it in theaters gave it a favorable 91% rating. Netflix could be vindicated when The Mosquito Bowl finally enters friendlier territory.

Stream the film on Wednesday, November 25, and stay tuned to Collider for more updates.
